newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures erode, end moderately lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures erode, end moderately lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures steadily eroded during spotty afternoon trading, finishing moderately lower and near session lows.
Traders cited a litany of reasons for the afternoon decline, including a market already awash in supplies, including this week's five- and two-year Treasury notes and ample corporate issues.

Some noted signs dealers may have been hedging inventory, while others also saw technical sales from funds as June Treasury bond futures slipped back below support areas in spurts of afternoon selling.
Hawkish comments by Federal Reserve governor Laurence Meyer added weight as well, brokers said.
He said the U.S. economy was growing at an unsustainably strong rate with solid momenum in the second quarter.
Meyer also said the unemployment rate has been inching lower and may have dropped below the non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment.

Also causing supply- and confidence-related jitters were Japanese press reports that Japan's Ministry of Finance was preparing an order to halt operations at Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co, floor brokers said.

But brokers said the market decided the Meyer comments were a convenient excuse to test the downside, since they discerned little new or unexpected in his speech. They also noted that June T-bond futures managed to return to the level where they had held when Meyer began speaking.
"If you look at the market reaction, we were at 107-15/32 prior to the Nissan story," said one floor broker. "On the Meyer coments, we were at 10/11 (107-10/32-11/32) and we're closing at 10."
The lack of constructive news about progress on the U.S. budget-pact front kept players leery of buying, they said.

June T-bonds caught a bid early Thursday after U.S. Senate minority leader Tom Daschle said there appears to be movement toward a budget accord. But Daschle later told reporters that it appeared "unlikely" as of today that a budget deal might be struck early next week.
Sales of June T-bonds accelerated when it pierced 107-14/32, last Thursday's low, and 107-11/32 area. It set day's low at 107-08/32, roughly 7-1/8 percent cash yield.
June T-bonds lost 13/32 to 107-10/32, notes lost 9/32 to 105-17/32, munis fell 11/32 to 112-09/32, Sept bills lost 0.040 to 94.265, Euros fell 0.045 to 93.690.
